instruction: click the <bell's top center> on the table

calls.reason: Probe left shoulder motion with a small absolute joint target to establish visible direction.
Bring the left arm gradually into the table view and close its gripper for a narrow pressing tip.
Adjust left base rotation toward the visible bell while retaining the raised approach.
Move the pressing tip inward toward the bell with a modest base rotation.
Continue inward alignment and raise the tip slightly while observing the bell in the wrist camera.
Probe elbow motion to establish how to bring the closed tip above the bell.
Test wrist pitch toward a downward pressing orientation while staying beside the bell.
Pitch the wrist downward using the observed sign of wrist rotation.
Advance the shoulder in a small increment to map tip position relative to the bell.
Raise the elbow while extending the shoulder, aiming to place the downward-facing tip over the table.
Tilt the pressing tip further downward and inspect its alignment in both cameras.
Adjust wrist roll to orient the pressing surface while keeping the arm beside the target.
Angle the wrist down toward the table using the direction observed in the prior wrist adjustment.
Extend the arm toward the bell while maintaining its downward wrist angle.
Sweep the downward-facing tip toward the bell’s depth on the table.
Increase reach while moving slightly forward to center the pressing tip on the bell.
Lift and extend the elbow to recover a clear above-table approach to the bell.
Align the visible tip laterally with the button using a small base rotation.
Rotate the wrist toward the bell so the wrist camera can resolve the pressing approach.
Shift the downward tip toward the button while limiting the vertical change.
Approach the button with a small coupled shoulder and elbow movement.
Lower the nearly aligned pressing tip in a small increment toward the top button.
Lift the tip angle slightly to align with the button top rather than the bell’s rim.
Fine-tune wrist alignment so the button approaches the visible tip in the wrist camera.
Lower the aligned tip a small amount while compensating wrist pitch to preserve its approach angle.
Make a short downward pressing movement at the bell’s top center.
Apply a small additional depression at the aligned bell button and inspect the result.
Correct the tip angle by a small amount to keep it centered on the moving top button.
Refine the pressing alignment by a small wrist increment at the button center.
Press downward gently while keeping the tip over the visible button center.
Continue the shallow center press with a small shoulder adjustment and elbow compensation.
Recenter the wrist on the button after the shallow descent.
Apply a final small pressing increment at the bell’s top center.
Track the button’s observed position with a small lift and reach correction.
Hold the centered pressing pose briefly to observe whether the button depresses.
Make a millimetric visual alignment correction at the button center.
Advance the pressing tip slightly while keeping the button centered in the wrist view.
Perform a short downward press while the tip is aligned over the bell button.
Adjust the final contact point toward the center of the exposed yellow button.
Center the pressing finger precisely on the button using a small wrist correction.
Press down at nearly constant reach with coupled shoulder, elbow, and wrist targets.
Briefly hold the pressing pose before releasing the bell button.
Lift the pressing tip clear of the bell to release the button and inspect its visible state.
Lower the raised left tip toward the current bell center with a short controlled approach.
Close the visible gap to the top button with a shallow elbow descent and wrist compensation.
Shift the tip slightly farther across the table to approach the center from above instead of the near edge.
Center the fingertip in the wrist view and apply a very small downward press.
Raise the elbow and orient the closed gripper more vertically for a clearer top-down press.
Continue steepening the pressing orientation while maintaining visible clearance above the bell.
Shift the steeply angled tip toward the button with a small shoulder movement.
Bring the steeply oriented finger over the button with coordinated base and elbow adjustments.
Recenter the visible pressing finger over the yellow top button.
Bring the downward-facing fingertip onto the top center using a small coordinated reach correction.
Move the right wrist camera modestly inward and down for an additional view of the bell and left fingertip.
Tilt the right camera upward slightly to include the left pressing finger above the bell.
Lower the left fingertip further; the side camera shows substantial clearance above the bell.
Frame both the left fingertip and the bell in the right camera for depth alignment.
Translate the left tip toward the bell while preserving wrist orientation, using the right camera to verify depth motion.
Translate the left arm across the remaining depth gap identified in the right camera.
Advance toward the bell while lifting the fingertip enough to clear the bell rim in the side view.
Continue the forward approach while raising the tip to the yellow button’s height in the right camera.
Move the fingertip forward and left over the bell using the two-camera alignment.
Advance and align the short pressing finger with the button, preserving clearance while closing the side-view gap.
Make a small lateral alignment correction while observing the remaining gap in both cameras.
Hold the current target briefly to distinguish settling motion from the commanded alignment change.
Close the remaining side-view gap with a small forward translation while keeping the finger orientation.
Continue the small forward correction, checking whether the arm still responds at this configuration.
Adjust the short pressing finger toward the top center while monitoring the side-view gap.
Lower and advance the fingertip together so the side-view gap closes at the top button.
Lower the finger with a small elbow-only adjustment, checking its actual side-view motion.
Reduce the elbow target into the previously responsive range after the last small change produced little visible motion.
Adjust the wrist’s lateral offset to align the finger with the button in both views.
Test a short shoulder descent while the finger is horizontally aligned with the button in the side view.
Rotate the closed pressing fingers slightly to expose a clearer downward contact surface.
Bring the rotated fingertip toward the button using the now-visible side-view contact surface.
Close the remaining horizontal gap between the rotated fingertip and the yellow button.
Bend the pressing wrist toward the button and recenter the side camera as the bell moves through its view.
Close the last visible lateral gap with small base and wrist adjustments while keeping the tip at button height.
Restore the previously stable wrist bend after the latest increment changed the approach angle unexpectedly.
Move the left arm away from the bell toward a less folded configuration before using the nearer right arm.
Bring the right arm inward and raise its closed fingertip toward the bell’s top-center approach.
Rotate the right arm inward so its fingertip enters the bell’s area in the head view.
Lift the right fingertip toward the bell’s height in the head view.
Extend the right shoulder to move the raised fingertip laterally over the bell.
Refine right-arm reach and partially open its fingers above the bell to make the contact geometry visible.
Close the right fingertips into a single pressing point and angle the left wrist camera toward the approach.
Angle the closed right fingertips downward toward the bell while retaining clearance.
Use the observed wrist direction to point the right fingertips down toward the table.
Roll the right wrist so its bend aims the closed tip toward the tabletop.
Correct wrist roll toward the table using the camera’s observed rotation.
Move the downward-facing right fingertip farther across the table toward the bell.
Align the right fingertip with the bell’s farther table position using base rotation and reach.
Aim the left wrist camera toward the bell to assess the right fingertip’s height before contact.
Center the bell and right fingertip in the left camera for a clearer height comparison.
Tilt the left camera toward the bell’s top and the approaching right fingers.
Lower the right fingertip from above the bell, using the left camera to check the remaining height.
Translate the lowered right fingertip farther across the table to the bell’s current position.
Advance the right arm’s reach while retaining its downward orientation, checking the side camera for approach.
Lower the right fingertip in a short increment toward the button’s visible center.
